note: Append-only. Ids are permanent: a case that no longer applies gets `retired` with a reason and keeps its number. Coverage is a CLAIM; scripts/case-registry.ts turns it into evidence by executing it.

cases.title: Prototype pollution through a request-supplied key
cases.rationale: A value the caller controls is used directly as a computed key on a write. Setting `__proto__` re-parents the object, which is the whole of CWE-1321. This is the shortest form the bug takes in real code.

cases.title: Prototype pollution through an unguarded merge helper
cases.rationale: `for (const k in src) dst[k] = src[k]` over a caller-supplied source is the shape behind the published prototype-pollution advisories in the deep-merge family. The key is never named in the source, so no allowlist can be read off the file.
cases.code: function merge(dst, src) { for (const k in src) { dst[k] = src[k]; } return dst; }

cases.title: A computed write onto `this` inside a class method
cases.rationale: Reads like noise and is not. Verified by execution: calling the method with `__proto__` re-parents the instance. Registered so the finding cannot be dismissed as an FP a second time.
cases.code: class Bag { set(k, v) { this[k] = v; } }

cases.title: Array append written as a self-indexed length
cases.rationale: NOT a defect. `arr.length` is a number, so the key cannot name a prototype slot. Written with `arr` as a PARAMETER on purpose: a locally-constructed array was already cleared by an older path, so `const arr = []` would pass whether or not the fix exists — a case that cannot fail is not evidence.

cases.title: A key iterated from a const array of string literals
cases.rationale: NOT a defect. Every value the key can take is written out in the same file and none is a dangerous property, so the question is decidable rather than assumed. An author who lists `__proto__` themselves still gets the report.
cases.code: const KEYS = ["alpha", "beta"]; const o = {}; for (const k of KEYS) { o[k] = 1; }

cases.title: A copy loop over an object the module itself owns
cases.rationale: NOT a defect. Nothing an attacker supplies reaches the loop. eslint-plugin-security reports this twice, once per side of the assignment; the noise is by their design, not a disagreement about the facts.
cases.code: const cfg = { a: 1 }; const out = {}; for (const k in cfg) { out[k] = cfg[k]; }

cases.title: A merge helper guarded by Object.hasOwn
cases.rationale: NOT a defect — it is the documented remediation for ILB-0002. Reporting the fix leaves the user with nothing to do, which is how a rule teaches people to disable it.
cases.code: function merge(dst, src) { for (const k in src) { if (Object.hasOwn(src, k)) dst[k] = src[k]; } }

cases.title: A timing-unsafe comparison of a bearer token
cases.rationale: `===` on a secret short-circuits at the first differing byte, so response time leaks the shared prefix. Observed guarding five HTTP endpoints in a real deployment.
cases.code:
import crypto from 'node:crypto';
function check(req, secret) { if (req.headers.authorization === secret) { return true; } return false; }

cases.title: An AST discriminant compared with ===
cases.rationale: NOT a defect. `node.kind === SyntaxKind.X` is a tag comparison, not a secret. Eleven findings in the wild came from this one shape before it was sealed.
cases.code:
import ts from 'typescript';
function f(node) { return node.kind === ts.SyntaxKind.ClassDeclaration; }

cases.title: Prototype pollution through a key reached by a call
cases.rationale: The key is computed at runtime by a function this file cannot summarise. Registered as an OPEN question rather than a claim: whether an unresolvable key should report is the same judgement as FP-010, and no rule currently answers it deliberately.
